feature: A text layer's box is its words
summary: Select a label and the blue box now sits on the letters on all four sides instead of hugging them at the top left and floating clear at the bottom right. W and H say how big the words are, so the number in the panel is the number you can measure on the picture.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: this is how a text layer reads everywhere now.

try.do: On a blank canvas, press T, click once and type Save changes, then press Command-Return.
Look at the blue box: the space between it and the letters should be the same on the left as on the right, and the same above as below.
Open the inspector and read W and H in Position & Size.
Type 100 into W and press Return. W reads 100 back and the words do not move.
Type a long sentence into a second label, then drag its right handle left until it takes two lines.
Put two labels 60 apart (Y 200 and Y 260), then measure the space between them with the Measure tool.
Check the caliper says 44, which is 260 minus 200 minus the 16 the H field reports.

evaluate: Does the box round a label look like it belongs to the words, or does it still sit slightly off on one side?
When you type a width into W, does the label end up as wide as you asked?
Do the numbers in the panel now agree with what a caliper measures on the same label?
Dragging a label's right edge in: does the handle feel like it is on the last letter?
Is a text box now too tight anywhere, so a letter looks cut off at an edge?
rough: The empty room is still in the box that gets saved. It had to be, or every text layer in every saved file would re-wrap. So this is the canvas, the panel, the magnets and the sweep band all speaking the box you can see, with one conversion at each door. Anything new that reads a text layer's box has to remember to do the same.

The narrowest a text box can be went from 80 to 84 in what is stored, so its WORDS floor at 80: that is what makes the panel able to say 'will not go below 80' truthfully. A text box that was already sitting on the old floor comes out four points wider and could gain back a wrapped line. Nothing else moves.

Found and not fixed: a short label typed on the canvas is 80 points wide even when its word is 46, because every inline text edit is given a minimum width. The labels inside the starter components hug their words instead, so the two disagree. Filed as its own task, 'A short label is as wide as its word'.

The caliper was never the problem: its feet snap to the edges detected in a picture and to other measurements, never to a layer's box, so it always read the space you can see. What changed is that the panel now agrees with it.
Screen Recording was granted, so every picture here is the window as a person sees it, not an offscreen render.
